name: edge-computing
context: Distributed computing paradigm that processes data near its source to reduce latency and bandwidth costs. Suitable for IoT, industrial control, retail, and scenarios requiring low-latency responses or offline operation. Moves computation and data storage closer to data sources rather than relying solely on centralized cloud data centers.
benefits: Ultra-low latency through local processing at data source
Significant bandwidth savings by filtering/aggregating before transmission
Offline operation capability independent of cloud connectivity
Enhanced data sovereignty for sensitive information
Reduced cloud ingestion costs (70-95% reduction possible)
tradeoffs: Higher operational complexity at fleet scale
Physical security concerns for distributed edge devices
Synchronization complexity and eventual consistency challenges
Difficult firmware/software updates across distributed nodes
use_cases: Real-time sensor processing with <10ms latency requirements
Video analytics at camera for object detection
Local ML inference for immediate decisions
Telemetry aggregation in high-frequency sensor estates
avoid_when: Strong consistency is required across all nodes
Data volumes are low and central processing is cost-effective
Reliable high-bandwidth connectivity is always available
Simple CRUD operations without time constraints
Batch processing workloads without real-time requirements
component_types: EdgeDevice: Computing at data source (sensors, cameras, wearables)
EdgeGateway: Protocol translation, local aggregation, buffering
EdgeNode: Compute cluster at edge location for running workloads
EdgeAnalyticsEngine: Local data processing and ML inference
LocalCache: Low-latency data access with eventual consistency
MessageBroker: Async communication and buffering between layers
DeviceManager: Fleet management, provisioning, health monitoring
ConfigurationAgent: Declarative config management, GitOps at edge
TelemetryCollector: Metrics, logs, traces aggregation with smart sampling
anti_patterns: Full cloud dependency for critical operations
Edge as miniature hyperscaler (forcing cloud patterns onto edge)
Chained synchronous calls at edge (latency compounds)
Static routing without site health awareness
design_principles: Design for Autonomy: Edge nodes must operate independently during cloud outages
Embrace Eventual Consistency: Strong consistency is impractical at scale across unreliable networks
Minimize Data Movement: Process locally, transmit only summaries and critical events
Standardize Operations: Use Kubernetes and GitOps everywhere for fleet management
Latency-Aware Routing: Prefer local decisions first, cloud only when necessary
Defense in Depth: Assume hostile environment with physical access and limited trust
best_practices: Hierarchical Processing: Match processing to appropriate edge layer (device → near → regional → cloud)
Durable Buffering: Use SSD-backed queues for store-and-forward; never use memory-only buffers
Smart Telemetry: Aggregate locally before transmitting; sample only what matters
Declarative Configuration: Use GitOps patterns for fleet-wide config management
Graceful Degradation: Implement circuit breakers and offline-first capabilities
Minimal Footprint: Use lightweight runtimes (Wasm, microVMs) on constrained devices
Zero-Trust Security: Implement mutual TLS, code signing, and hardware attestation
Horizontal Scaling: Deploy edge nodes in pairs for critical workloads with automatic failover
